---
title: "Research, Publications & Software"
---

The Open Data Lab develops open-source software, educational resources, and public-facing research that make civic data more accessible through reproducible workflows.

Together, these projects form a connected ecosystem where students, educators, researchers, and practitioners can learn, build, publish, and contribute using the same open tools.

Whenever possible, Lab projects are developed as open educational or open-source resources, with publicly available code, documentation, and archived releases.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Featured Projects

### NYC Open Data Student Gallery {#sec-nyc-opendata-student-gallery}

The NYC Open Data Student Gallery showcases graduate student research developed using NYC Open Data. Each project investigates a unique question about New York City through reproducible analysis, visualization, and data storytelling.

The Gallery demonstrates how classroom work can become public scholarship with lasting value.

**Resources**

- 📖 [Explore the Student Gallery](https://martinezc1-nyc-open-data-student-gallery.share.connect.posit.cloud/)
- 💻 [Source Code (GitHub)](https://github.com/martinezc1/NYC-Open-Data-Student-Gallery)
- 📦 [Archived Release (Zenodo)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21397679)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### OpenData Package Developer's Guide {#sec-opendata-developers-guide}

The OpenData Package Developer's Guide provides a complete framework for building city-specific R packages that interface with Socrata-based open data portals.

The guide includes reusable package templates, implementation tutorials, development best practices, and documentation for creating open-source tools that follow a consistent design across cities.

**Resources**

- 📖 [Read the Guide](https://martinezc1-the-opendata-package-developers-guide.share.connect.posit.cloud/)
- 💻 [Source Code (GitHub)](https://github.com/martinezc1/OpenDataPackageGuide)
- 📦 [Archived Release (Zenodo)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21383609)

## Software

The Lab develops open-source R packages that provide a unified interface for accessing and analyzing public data. Together, these packages form a growing ecosystem designed to make civic data more accessible, reproducible, and consistent across multiple open data portals.

Each package follows the same design philosophy, allowing users to browse datasets, retrieve data, and work with multiple open data portals using a familiar workflow.

The ecosystem is anchored by `nycOpenData`, which established the architecture and development standards that now guide every package in the collection.

### The Foundation of the Package Ecosystem

The Open Data package ecosystem was built on the architecture established by `nycOpenData`, the Lab's flagship R package for accessing NYC Open Data.

In 2026, `nycOpenData` successfully completed the independent software peer-review process conducted by **rOpenSci**, recognizing the package for its documentation, testing, usability, and adherence to open-source best practices.

Rather than developing each new package independently, the Lab uses the peer-reviewed design of `nycOpenData` as the foundation for every subsequent package. The [**OpenData Package Developer's Guide**](#sec-opendata-developers-guide) provides a standardized framework for implementing this architecture across new city and state packages.

As additional city packages are developed, they inherit the same underlying design principles, making it easier for users to transition between data portals while relying on a familiar and reproducible workflow.

## Current Initiatives

### NYC 311 Dashboard {#sec-nyc-311-dashboard}

The Open Data Lab is developing an interactive dashboard that makes NYC 311 data easier to explore and understand. Using NYC Open Data and reproducible workflows, the project will allow users to investigate patterns in service requests across the city through accessible visualizations and interactive tools.

The dashboard is currently being developed by Civic Data Application Development Intern [**Emma V. Tupone**](../current-members/emma-tupone.qmd).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### CUNY Sports Analytics Initiative {#sec-cuny-sports-analytics}

The Open Data Lab is building a student-driven sports analytics initiative that uses real collegiate athletics data to support CUNY coaches, players, and teams.

Students can contribute through sports analytics or data development, working on projects such as scouting reports, performance analysis, data visualization, database development, and reproducible analytical workflows.

[Apply to the CUNY Sports Analytics Team](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdRmNDdMDB9ZJb2ZIJGHAzfwBdY25dl-Co0h42UarCo8MJx8g/viewform?usp=header){.btn .btn-primary}
